brim.name: Brim
brim.summary: A child pulled out of the sea at Wrackhead who does not speak and does not age as children do, and whom the coast folk have decided is the last of the kings of Kell; held in place, like the crown, by being believed in.
brim.body:
## Who

Eleven years ago, in the grey, on a still day at low water, [[rauk]] came up from Old
[[kell]] with a child under one arm that had not been there when she went down. It was
perhaps three. It is perhaps nine now, and it should be fourteen. It has never spoken. It
has salt-white eyes that see in the dark and a habit of looking at the sea as if waiting for
someone to finish a sentence.

## What the coast decided

The coast folk decided, without a meeting, that the child was the last of the kings of Kell,
given back. They call it Brim, which is the name [[vell]] gave it, and they leave fish at
Rauk's door. Nobody has proved a word of it. Nobody has needed to. It is believed, and in the
Mark that is a kind of iron.

## In the world

- The [[greycloaks]] have offered to foster the child at the fort on [[wrackhead]]. Rauk
  declined. The offer stands, and is polite.
- Since [[the-ebb]] the child has walked to the waterline every morning and stood where the
  quay-stones are showing, and the water has been a little further out each time.
- [[sarn]], asked about the child, did not change the subject. That is the only time.

## Threads

- If the child is the king, whose is the crown?
- If it is not, what came up with it?

drusk.name: Drusk
drusk.summary: The Greycloak captain of the bridge at Hookford, who carries the hook Tolm does not and hangs the tithe-books from it; the order's ledger-keeper, and the one who reads the longest list at Hangmoot.
drusk.body:
## Who

Drusk holds the bridge at [[hookford]], and with it the tithe-books of the middle Mark. He
is the Greycloak who carries a hook, keeps it sharp, and has used it twice; he says the
second time was the last. He is younger than [[tolm]], and where Tolm apologises, Drusk
writes it down. The order finds the two of them useful in the same way a smith finds a
hammer and a file useful, and has never put them in one room.

## The books

Every tithe in the middle Mark goes into Drusk's books, and the books hang from the hooks on
the bridge where the town can see them. He reads from them at the Rope-Moot on
[[hangmoot]], politely, and his is the longest list. The hangmen say his books are a poor
copy of a ledger older than [[kell]], and Drusk has never asked which.

## In the world

- He has never met [[gorvek]]. He has written the price on Gorvek's head into the books
  every winter since the grey, in the same hand.
- He was the first Greycloak to ask, in writing, why Tolm let a man go at the
  [[wallgate]]. He has not had an answer, and has not asked again.
- Since [[the-ebb]] the books have a new column. He has not said what it counts.

## Threads

- What did the hook do the second time?

gorvek.name: Gorvek
gorvek.summary: A barbarian of Bonereach who walked out of the Ashfall with iron in his hand and wants of a stream only that it obeys.
gorvek.body:
## Who

Gorvek is what [[bonereach]] makes of the ones it does not kill. He was a boy when the grey
came down; he was a man when it lifted, and nobody in the village he walked back into asked
him what he had eaten in between. He is broad, scarred along the left forearm where a
Greycloak's hook took a strip of him, and quiet in the way of people who have decided that
most words are a kind of cowardice.

His hands are scarred by fire, and he does not say which fire. He rides a grey mare he has
not named, because naming is river-priest work.

He does not read. He does not need to. He has a gift for knowing when a thing is lying to
him, and machines lie less than men, which is why he tolerates them.

## Voice

Gorvek speaks in creeds: short, physical, in the present tense. He answers questions with
what he wants, not with what he thinks. He never explains a joke and rarely makes one on
purpose. When he swears, he swears by the Ashfall, never by a god; he has met the river-priests
of [[thurn]] and was not impressed.

He is the hero of the stories, not their narrator. That is [[sarn]]'s work, and Gorvek knows
it and dislikes it.

## In the world

- He carries [[streamlord]] and does not know what it is, only what it does.
- He has killed Greycloaks and will again. The [[greycloaks]] have a price on him that they
  raise every winter and never pay.
- He has met Sarn three times and seen a face none of the times.
- He walked out of the grey beside [[vurn]], who tells the sagas Gorvek will not, and reads
  him the ledger [[linelord]] that he says he does not need.

## Threads

- What did he eat in the Ashfall?
- Who taught him that a stream can be told to stop?

kesk.name: Kesk
kesk.summary: The smith on the shingle below the fort at Wrackhead, who sells iron to everyone going down into Kell and buys back whatever comes up, and has not asked a question in eleven years.
kesk.body:
## Who

Kesk keeps a forge on the shingle at [[wrackhead]], between the salt-pile and the fort,
which is the only ground on the Head that nobody else wants. Hooks, knives, axes, lamp-cages,
and mail with the grey dye scrubbed out of it: the [[greycloaks]] lose men on the
[[quaysteps]] and Kesk does not ask how the mail gets to him. Since [[the-ebb]] the forge has
not gone cold.

## Voice

Prices. Kesk says the price, then the price again, slower, and then nothing. Ask him where
something came from and he tells you what it weighs.

## In the world

- He buys back what comes up out of [[kell]] at a third of what he sells it for, and the
  coast says that is fair, because he is the one who has to sell it to the fort.
- [[rauk]] has never bought from him. He has never asked her why.

nask.name: Nask
nask.summary: The last river-priest born in Kell, who was a boy on the quay the night Sarn came, and who has walked the drowned coast naming what the sea gives up ever since.
nask.body:
## Who

Nask was born in [[kell]] when Kell had streets, and was on the quay the night the
[[iron-crown-of-kell]] lost its stones. He was nine. He saw the water come up the steps
and he did not see a face. He is old now, bent, and wet to the hip rather than the knee,
because the coast is where he walks and the coast is where the sea takes back what it
gave.

## The names

Nask names what washes up. A plank, a bone, a child. He gave [[sarn]] no name; that was the
priests upriver, and he has said it was the right name and the wrong year. He taught
[[vell]] the names of the two rivers and was not consulted when Vell named [[the-ebb]]. He
has said nothing about that, at length.

## Voice

Names, never reasons, and slower than the young ones. Nask will answer a question the
following morning, on the shingle, with the name written in the wet sand, and let the tide
take it.

## In the world

- He goes down to the salt-pile at [[wrackhead]] once a year and names it, and the coast
  folk do not ask him to stop.
- He named the ledger the coast calls [[linelord]], and then did what the river-priests do
  with the things they name: he stopped talking about it.

## Threads

- What did Nask see on the quay that was not a face?

osk.name: Osk
osk.summary: The sorcerer who stayed in the grey when it lifted and sells what she found there from the rim of Greyhollow; every price is a thing you did not know you had.
osk.body:
## Who

Osk went into the grey a midwife and came out of it something the Ashborn will not put a
word to. She is not old. She looks it in some lights. She lives on the rim of [[greyhollow]]
in a house with its back to the mist, and she goes in when she pleases, which is the thing
nobody else can do.

## What she sells

Things from the grey: a name you lost in it, a winter you do not remember, the last thing a
dead man said. She takes payment in kind, and what she takes is always something you did not
know you had until it was gone. The [[river-priests]] say this makes her a thief. Osk says it
makes her a merchant, and asks what the difference is, and the priests do not have a name
for it.

## Voice

Osk explains. She is the only one in the Mark who does, and it is the most frightening thing
about her. Everything she says is true, checkable, and slightly too much.

## In the world

- She says she has seen [[sarn]]'s face and forgotten it on purpose. Nobody can prove either
  half.
- She has offered [[gorvek]] the answer to what he ate in the grey. He walked away. She says
  he will be back, and that this is not a threat.
- [[tolm]] will not tithe her. The [[greycloaks]] have not asked him why.
- Since [[the-ebb]] she has begun selling things she says came up out of [[kell]].

## Threads

- What did Osk find in the grey that made her stay?
- Does she know where a ruby is?

rauk.name: Rauk
rauk.summary: The wrecker of Wrackhead who has dived Old Kell more times than anyone alive, touched the iron crown on the drowned king's head, and come up each time with less to say.
rauk.body:
## Who

Rauk is the best diver on the drowned coast, which means the best in the Mark, which means
the only one who has gone down through the iron roof of [[kell]]'s hall and come back up.
She is salt-marked: white lines on her arms where the deep cold got in and stayed. She is
not tall. She has broken a Greycloak's arm on the shingle at [[wrackhead]] and been forgiven
for it, which is rarer than the dive.

## The crown

She has touched the [[iron-crown-of-kell]]. It is still on the king. She says the three
sockets are empty and cold and the iron is warm, and she says nothing else about it, and she
has stopped going down. The coast folk say [[vorr]] told her something. Rauk says the sea
does not talk. It keeps.

## Voice

Rauk speaks like a diver: short, between breaths, saving the air. She does not swear by the
Ashfall, which never reached the coast. She swears by the pile.

## In the world

- She pulled [[brim]] out of the water at Wrackhead eleven years ago and has kept the child
  since, and does not say what else came up with it.
- Since [[the-ebb]] the [[greycloaks]] have offered her the fort's weight in coin to go down
  once more. She has said no in a way they have accepted.

## Threads

- What is the warm iron?
- Why has she stopped diving now that diving is getting easier?

sarn.name: Sarn
sarn.summary: A faceless thief-demon every soul in Gallowmark can name and none has seen; stole the rubies of the Iron Crown and now narrates the grimoire with a smile nobody can find.
sarn.body:
## What

Nobody agrees on whether Sarn is a woman, a man, or a thing that has decided it is a person.
The stories agree on three points: Sarn has no face that anyone remembers a minute after
seeing it, Sarn has yellow eyes that they remember for the rest of their lives, and Sarn
took the three rubies out of the [[iron-crown-of-kell]] in a single night, after which the
city of [[kell]] came apart the way a rope does when the one strand that mattered is cut.

The river-priests of [[thurn]] call Sarn the Lord of Streams. It is not a compliment. It is
the name you give a thing that goes where water goes and takes what water takes.

## Voice

Sarn narrates. Sarn tempts, instructs, and never raises its voice. Sentences are short and
end where the knife goes in. Sarn addresses the reader directly ("Sit. Read.") and offers
gifts that are actually thefts: *I will take one thing from you.* Sarn never lies outright
and never tells the whole truth. When Sarn is generous, ask why.

Sarn is the voice of every grimoire in Gallowmark that is worth reading, including the one
that teaches the use of [[streamlord]].

## In the world

- Sarn haunts [[gallowmark]] the way a rumour does: everywhere at once, never in the room.
- The [[greycloaks]] have tried to hire Sarn and to kill Sarn. Both attempts are ongoing.
- Sarn has spoken to [[gorvek]] three times. Gorvek remembers only the eyes.

## Threads

- Where are the three rubies now?
- What does Sarn actually want from the reader?

tolm.name: Tolm
tolm.summary: The Greycloak captain who sits in the door of the Wallgate toll-house; has taken forty villages without drawing a blade, and is sorry about every one of them.
tolm.body:
## Who

Tolm is the Greycloak the stories mean when they say a captain rides in alone and sits down.
He is fifty, thin, grey before the cloak was, and polite in the way of a man who has never
once been refused. He does not carry a hook. He says he is no good with it, which is true,
and that he does not need one, which is also true. He keeps the toll-house at [[wallgate]]
and has kept it since the grey.

## Voice

Tolm apologises. He apologises for the tithe, the weather, the price on [[gorvek]]'s head
and the fact that it will be raised again in winter. Every apology is sincere and none of
them changes anything. Ask him a question and he will thank you for it.

## In the world

- He has taken forty villages through the open gate. He remembers every one by the name of
  the person who let him in.
- He has met Gorvek once, across the toll-house table, and let him go. The [[greycloaks]]
  have not asked why. He is waiting for them to.
- He does not go near [[greyhollow]], and is the only Greycloak who will say so.
- Since [[the-ebb]] the order has sent him south for the first time. He apologised to the
  toll-house.

## Threads

- What did Tolm let through the Wallgate that he should not have?

vell.name: Vell
vell.summary: The barefoot river-priest of Hookford who named the Ebb before anyone had seen the water move, and who answers every question with a name.
vell.body:
## Who

Vell was born under the bridge at [[hookford]] and has not worn a shoe since. He is young
for a river-priest, wet to the knee like the rest, and unwelcome at every table in town
except the ones with a death in the family. He walks the two rivers from the ford to the
coast and back each season, and he keeps the names.

## The naming

When the water first went out from Old [[kell]], the coast folk sent to the [[river-priests]]
for a name. Vell had already given it. He had stood on the bridge at Hookford a month before
and said the word *Ebb* to the river, and the river had gone down a finger under his feet.
He says this is not prophecy. He says a name is a grip, and he took hold of something before
it had finished happening.

## Voice

Names, never reasons. Ask Vell why the sea is going out and he will say [[vorr]]. Ask him
what to do and he will say [[thurn]]. Ask him what [[sarn]] wants and he will look at you a
long time and say your own name.

## In the world

- He named [[the-ebb]], and the river-priests are not sure he had the right.
- He has met [[gorvek]] and named the thing Gorvek carries to his face. Gorvek did not
  thank him.
- He named the child at [[wrackhead]] [[brim]], and would not say why.

## Threads

- What name did Vell give the ninth gallows at [[hangmoot]], and why did the Reeve pay him
  for it?

vurn.name: Vurn
vurn.summary: The other one who walked out of the Ashfall beside Gorvek; the one who talks, and who tells the sagas of the Reach in the alehouse at Hookford while Gorvek says nothing.
vurn.body:
## Who

Two walked out of the grey into the same village on the same morning. One was [[gorvek]].
The other was Vurn, who was thinner, louder, and had kept count of the days. The elders of
[[bonereach]] asked them both what they wanted. Gorvek's answer became a creed. Vurn's
answer was *ale*, and the Reach has liked him for it since.

## The telling

Vurn tells the sagas. He tells them at [[hookford]] for drink, on the ridge at
[[hangmoot]] for free, and in Bonereach to children who have heard them before. They are
the sagas of the Reach: what a warrior wants, what a warrior does, and what he says when
the work is done. Half of them are Gorvek's deeds and the other half are Vurn's, and Vurn
has been honest about which is which exactly once, and was drunk.

## Voice

Vurn speaks in the cadence of the sagas because he made it. Loud, physical, present tense,
with a boast at the end where Gorvek would have put nothing. He swears by the Ashfall, like
Gorvek, and also by ale, mead, the Reach, and anything else within reach.

## In the world

- He reads. He reads the ledger [[linelord]] aloud to Gorvek, who says he does not need it
  and listens to every line.
- He has met [[sarn]] once, and told the story forty times, and it is different every time,
  and the eyes are always yellow.

## Threads

- What did Vurn count in the grey, and why did he stop at the number he stopped at?

bonereach.name: Bonereach
bonereach.summary: The northern reach of Gallowmark, a country of scree, bone-white birch and villages that count their dead in winters; where the Ashfall fell hardest and Gorvek was born.
bonereach.body:
## The reach

Bonereach is the part of [[gallowmark]] nobody wanted and somebody kept. Scree slopes, birch
so pale it looks skinned, and villages built into the lee of rocks because the wind comes
off the Wallmountains with an opinion. The people of the Reach are the people of the Mark
boiled down: fewer words, harder hands, a longer memory.

## Since the Ashfall

The [[the-ashfall]] fell here first and lifted here last. The Reach lost half its villages
and does not say which half. Those who walked out of the grey, [[gorvek]] among them, are
called the Ashborn behind their backs and never to their faces.

## Custom

The elders of the Reach do not ask a returning warrior where he has been. They ask what he
wants. The answer is the man.

brinevaults.name: The Brinevaults
brinevaults.summary: The cellars, cisterns and counting-vaults under the iron hall, where Kell kept its salt, its coin and its dead, all three packed the same way.
brinevaults.body:
## The vaults

Kell was rich in two things, salt and records, and it kept both under the hall. The
Brinevaults are rooms of salt cut from salt: cisterns, cellars, and long low counting-rooms
where clerks copied the ledger [[linelord]] by lamplight. Kell salted its dead and shelved
them here too, because salt keeps and the city believed in keeping.

## Since the Ebb

The vaults were the last of Kell to be under water and are the last to come out of it. The
salt has drunk the sea for forty years and is still wet. What was shelved here is
[[the-salted]] now. The ropes that hang down the cistern shafts are pulled taut toward the
hall, and nobody at [[wrackhead]] has gone far enough to see what pulls them.

## Threads

- Where are Kell's copies of the ledger? The clerks made many.

gallowmark.name: Gallowmark
gallowmark.summary: The land itself; a march of gallows, grey rivers and stubborn people between the mountains and the drowned coast, where the Ashfall fell and never quite lifted.
gallowmark.body:
## The land

Gallowmark is named for what its first rulers built before they built anything else. The
gallows are still there on the ridges, most of them empty, none of them taken down. The land
runs from the Wallmountains in the north to the drowned coast in the south, cut through by
grey rivers that the priests of [[thurn]] say are one river pretending to be many. The
gallows belong to [[hask]]; the sea at the end of the rivers belongs to [[vorr]]. Nobody
prays to any of the three. They keep out of the way.

Nothing here is fertile by accident. The people are hard because the soil is, and they trust
what they can hold. A stranger who can make a thing obey will be respected; a stranger who
explains why will be watched.

## Regions

- [[bonereach]] in the north, where [[gorvek]] comes from.
- [[kell]] on the coast, the drowned city that still counts as a place because the survivors
  refuse to stop saying its name.
- [[wallgate]] in the far north, the one pass through the Wallmountains and the one gate
  nobody can close.
- [[hookford]] in the middle Mark, where two rivers meet and the only market is.
- [[hangmoot]] above it, the ridge of nine gallows where the Mark pays its debts.
- [[greyhollow]] in the eastern hills, where the Ashfall never lifted.
- [[wrackhead]] on the coast, the headland over Old Kell.

## Since the Ashfall

The [[the-ashfall]] came down over the north and stayed a generation. The Mark has been
darker since, and its stories shorter.

## Since the Ebb

In the first winter after the grey lifted the sea began to go out from Old Kell. [[the-ebb]]
is pulling every road in the Mark toward the coast, and the Mark is going.

greyhollow.name: Greyhollow
greyhollow.summary: A hollow in the eastern hills where the Ashfall never lifted; the grey stands in it like milk in a bowl, and what walks out is never quite what walked in.
greyhollow.body:
## The hollow

East of the middle Mark the hills fold, and in one fold the grey stayed. From the rim you
can see it: [[the-ashfall]], a generation late, lying in the hollow like milk in a bowl and
not moving with the wind. The birch at the edge are white on the outside and black on the
inside. Nobody farms within a mile of it.

## Going in

People go in. Some for what they lost in the grey, some for what [[osk]] sells, some because
the [[greycloaks]] do not go in and that is worth a great deal. Those who come out come out
changed in a way nobody can name, and the [[river-priests]] have refused to try. [[gorvek]]
has never said whether he has been back.

## What it is

The Ashborn say the Hollow is the last of the grey. Osk says it is the first, and that the
rest of the Ashfall was only spillage.

## Threads

- Does the grey in the Hollow rise when the sea goes out?

hangmoot.name: Hangmoot
hangmoot.summary: The ridge of nine gallows above the middle Mark where the land's first rulers hanged their god, and where once a year at the Rope-Moot every debt in Gallowmark is paid, forgiven or hanged.
hangmoot.body:
## The ridge

Nine gallows on a bare ridge, older than [[kell]], taller than anything else the first rulers
built. Eight of them are used. The ninth has never held anyone that anyone will name, and it
is the one the wind plays. This is where [[hask]] hangs, if he hangs anywhere.

## The Rope-Moot

Once a year, when the rivers are lowest, the Mark comes up the ridge. Debts are read out by
the Reeve. What can be paid is paid. What cannot is hanged or forgiven, and the Mark has
always found the first cheaper. The [[greycloaks]] attend, politely, and read the longest
list.

## The slack rope

The hangmen say one of the nine ropes has hung slack since [[the-drowning-of-kell]], and
that a slack rope is a debt nobody has collected. Since [[the-ebb]] the Reeve has had the
ninth gallows re-roped, and the Mark noticed.

## Threads

- Whose name is on the ninth gallows?
- Who is the Reeve, and who was the Reeve before?

hookford.name: Hookford
hookford.summary: The one town in the middle Mark, where two of the grey rivers meet at a ford and the Greycloaks hang their tithe-books from hooks on the bridge; market, tithe-house, and the last warm bed before anywhere.
hookford.body:
## The town

Two of the three grey rivers meet at Hookford. The ford was there before the town, and the
bridge before the [[greycloaks]]. It is the only place in the middle Mark with a market, a
smith who takes coin, and a hall where a stranger can sleep with a door between him and the
wind. The people of the Mark distrust it accordingly.

## The hooks

The Greycloaks hung their hooks on the bridge the year they came, one per span, and hang the
tithe-books from them. Nobody has ever been hanged from the bridge. Everybody knows that they
could be, and pays.

## The road

Every road in the Mark passes through Hookford: down from [[wallgate]] and [[bonereach]], up
from [[wrackhead]] and the coast, east to the rim of [[greyhollow]], and the ridge road to
[[hangmoot]]. If [[the-ebb]] pulls the Mark to the coast, it will pull it through here.

## Threads

- Who owned the bridge before the hooks?

kell.name: Kell
kell.summary: The old royal city on the drowned coast, seat of the Iron Crown, which came apart the night Sarn took the rubies and has been sinking ever since.
kell.body:
## The city

Kell was the only city in [[gallowmark]] that deserved the word. Stone quays, a hall with a
roof of iron plates, and a king with a crown that held the three rivers in place: that is
how the river-priests tell it, and they tell it with their hands over their mouths.

The last king kept the ledger [[linelord]] in the iron-roofed hall and read it the winter
before the night, looking for a wall that would hold. Brother [[nask]] was a boy on the quay.

## The night

Then [[sarn]] came, and the [[iron-crown-of-kell]] lost its three rubies in one night, and by
morning the quays were under water and the king was under the quays. Whether the crown held
the sea back or only the people's belief that it did, the result is the same: Kell is a place
you sail over.

## Now

Old Kell is a name the coast people still use for the water where the city was. The
[[greycloaks]] say they will raise it. They have said so for forty years.

lowstreets.name: The Lowstreets
lowstreets.summary: The streets of drowned Kell under forty years of silt, where the houses still stand with their doors shut from the inside.
lowstreets.body:
## The streets

Below [[quaysteps]] the city is still a city. The streets run where they ran, half full of
silt and wreck, and the houses stand along them with their roofs gone and their doors shut.
Shut from the inside. The coast folk say Kell did not run that night. It went home, barred
the door, and waited for the crown to hold.

## What lives here

What the sea did not keep, it gave to the things that eat. What it did keep stands in the
doorways: [[the-kept]], who wake when the flood comes and walk with it. The pickers of
[[wrackhead]] work the Lowstreets in pairs and leave a rope back to the steps, and the
rope is the thing they trust.

## Threads

- What did Kell bar its doors against, if not the water?

quaysteps.name: The Quaysteps
quaysteps.summary: The stone quays and water-stairs of drowned Kell, the first ground the Ebb gave back, where the coast goes picking at low water and does not always come up.
quaysteps.body:
## The steps

Kell met the sea in stairs. Broad stone steps went down from every street to the water, and
the water came up them twice a day to meet the city halfway. Now the city is under the
steps and the steps are under the weed, and since [[the-ebb]] the top of them shows at low
water below [[wrackhead]], green and slick and going down.

This is the first of drowned [[kell]], and the shallowest. Boats rot on the quay where they
were tied. Bollards stand in rows with the ropes still on them. Everything here has been
picked once already.

## The tide

The sea goes out further every month, but it still comes back twice a day. At low water
the quays are a place you can walk. At the flood they are a place you drown. The coast folk
who go down count their steps and count the time, and the ones who forget one of the two
are kept.

## Threads

- Who tied the boats, the night before?

the-iron-hall.name: The Iron Hall
aliases: the King's Hall, the Hall under the Roof
the-iron-hall.summary: The hall of the last king of Kell under its roof of iron plates, where the king still sits with the empty crown, the ledger is still on its stand, and the one who keeps is underneath.
the-iron-hall.body:
## The hall

The iron roof is the only part of [[kell]] the coast can see: for an hour on a still day at
low water it stands clear of the salt below [[wrackhead]], and since [[the-ebb]] the hour
gets longer. Under it is the hall. The king sits where he sat. [[rauk]] has touched the
[[iron-crown-of-kell]] on his head and come up saying the iron is warm.

## The ledger

The last king read [[linelord]] in this hall the winter before the night, looking for a wall
that would hold. It is still here, open on its stand at the king's right hand,
heavier than a man can carry far and lighter than it ought to be. Whoever takes it up has to
go out the only way the hall leaves open: up, through a gap in the iron roof, at low water.

## Underneath

Below the hall floor is the drain the Ebb runs out through, and in it is [[the-salt-mouth]].
The river-priests do not name it. The coast folk say it is what [[vorr]] keeps his mouth
with.

## Threads

- Is the ledger here, or a copy the clerks made? This draft answers the thread on [[linelord]]; canon has not.
- What is the warm iron?

wallgate.name: Wallgate
wallgate.summary: The one pass through the Wallmountains, a throat of black rock with a Greycloak toll-house in it; the only gate into Gallowmark from the north, and the one nobody can close.
wallgate.body:
## The pass

The Wallmountains have one gap, and the Mark calls it the Wallgate because nobody in the
Mark wastes a second word. It is a throat of black rock a day's walk long, with the first of
the grey rivers coming down through it cold enough to stop a heart. North of it is whatever
the Ashfall came from. South of it is [[bonereach]].

## The toll-house

The [[greycloaks]] hold the Wallgate the way they hold everything: one house, one captain,
one open door. [[tolm]] sits in it. Nobody has ever taken the Wallgate by force, because
nobody has ever needed to. It is a gate that cannot be shut, and the order likes those.

## What comes through

Since the grey lifted, things come down out of the north through the Wallgate that did not
before. The toll-house tithes them like anyone else.

## Threads

- What is north of the Wallgate?
- Why does the first river run warm for one night each winter?

wrackhead.name: Wrackhead
wrackhead.summary: The headland over the drowned city, where the Greycloaks' first fort stands, the coast folk keep the salt-pile for Vorr, and the wreckers dive Old Kell for what the sea has not kept.
wrackhead.body:
## The head

A black headland shaped like a fist, with Old [[kell]] under the water at its knuckles. The
[[greycloaks]] built their first fort here, forty years ago, to guard the drowned quays. It
is the smallest fort they hold and the only one they have never left.

## The salt-pile

Below the fort, on the shingle, the coast folk keep a pile of wreck-wood and salt for
[[vorr]]. A plank from every wreck, a handful from every net. The Greycloaks tithe
everything on the coast and have never touched the pile.

## The wreckers

The people of Wrackhead dive. On a still day at low water you can see the iron roof of
Kell's hall, and once a year somebody goes down to it. [[rauk]] has gone down more than
anyone, come up with less each time, and stopped talking about it.

## Since the Ebb

The water is going out. The quays are showing. Since [[the-ebb]] the fort has doubled its
garrison and the salt-pile has doubled in height, and neither side has said why.

## Threads

- What is the fort really guarding: Kell, or the pile?

greycloaks.name: The Greycloaks
greycloaks.summary: The grey-cloaked order that holds Gallowmark by taking villages through the one gate left open; tithe-collectors, hook-wielders, and the only law most of the Mark has seen.
greycloaks.body:
## What they are

The Greycloaks began as the men who guarded the drowned quays of [[kell]] so that nobody
would steal what the sea had not yet taken. Forty years on, they guard everything, and what
they guard they tithe. Their cloaks are grey because grey hides ash, and the order was born
in the [[the-ashfall]].

## How they take a village

Never by storm. A Greycloak captain rides in alone, finds the one gate left open, and sits
down inside it. By evening the village is paying tithe and thinks it decided to. Every siege
in Gallowmark has been lost this way, which is why the wise close every gate, including the
ones they cannot see.

## The books

What the order tithes it writes down. The tithe-books hang from the hooks on the bridge at
[[hookford]], in Captain [[drusk]]'s hand, and the hangmen say they are a poor copy of the
ledger [[linelord]]. Captain [[tolm]] keeps the [[wallgate]] and writes nothing down.

## Enemies

[[gorvek]] has a price on his head that the order raises every winter. [[sarn]] they have tried
to hire and to kill, and the order's own records disagree on which came first.

river-priests.name: The River-Priests of Thurn
river-priests.summary: The barefoot priesthood of the river-god Thurn, keepers of the names, who alone dare call Sarn the Lord of Streams and who say all the grey rivers are one.
river-priests.body:
## Who they are

Barefoot, wet to the knee, and unwelcome at most tables, the river-priests walk the banks of
the grey rivers of [[gallowmark]] and keep the names of things. They hold that every stream
in the Mark is the same river, [[thurn]], pretending to be many, and that to name a thing
truly is to have a grip on it.

## The naming

It was the river-priests who named [[sarn]] the Lord of Streams, and they meant it as a
warning: here is the thing that goes where water goes. They also named the artifact that
[[gorvek]] carries. They called it [[streamlord]], and then they stopped talking about it.

## Custom

A river-priest will answer any question with a name, and never with a reason.

hask.name: Hask
hask.summary: The hanged god of the gallows on the ridges; the first rulers of the Mark hanged him so the land would hold, and every debt in Gallowmark is still paid at his rope.
hask.body:
## The god

[[gallowmark]] is named for the gallows, and the gallows are for Hask. The first rulers of
the Mark, before [[kell]] had a quay, built nine gallows on a ridge and hanged their god on
the ninth so the land would hold. That is the story the hangmen tell, and they tell it with
the knot already tied. Hask did not die. A hanged god does not; he hangs. Everything owed in
the Mark is owed to the rope, and the rope is his.

## The debt

Hask is the god of what is owed. A tithe is a debt, an oath is a debt, a name given is a
debt. The [[greycloaks]] have never written Hask's name in a ledger, and they collect in his
shape: patiently, and once. Hask has no priests. He has hangmen, and the Reeve of
[[hangmoot]] is the first among them.

## The rope and the crown

The hangmen say the land is held in place by nine ropes and one iron ring, and that the night
[[sarn]] emptied the [[iron-crown-of-kell]] one of the nine went slack. They do not say which.
Since [[the-ebb]] they have stopped saying nothing.

## Threads

- Is Hask the god the Greycloaks do not name, or the god they are afraid of?
- Whom did the first rulers hang, really?

thurn.name: Thurn
thurn.summary: The river-god of Gallowmark, the one grey river that pretends to be many; cold, patient, and the only god whose priests are taken seriously by people who trust nothing.
thurn.body:
## The god

Thurn does not have a face, a temple, or a promise. Thurn has water, and water goes where it
goes. The people of [[gallowmark]] do not pray to Thurn; they keep out of the way. The
[[river-priests]] say this is the correct form of worship.

## Streams

Everything that flows is Thurn's, in the priests' telling: rivers, blood, rumour, and the
thing that moves between a server and a browser when [[streamlord]] is used. A stream that
obeys a man is a piece of the god held still, and the priests are of two minds about whether
that is a blasphemy or the whole point.

## Threads

- Does Thurn mind that [[sarn]] has been called Lord of Streams?

vorr.name: Vorr
vorr.summary: The drowned god of the salt deep below the coast, who keeps what the sea takes and took Kell whole; the coast folk pay him in wreckage and do not ask for anything back.
vorr.body:
## The god

[[thurn]] is what flows. Vorr is where it stops. The [[river-priests]] say every grey river
is one river; the coast folk say yes, and it ends in Vorr's mouth. Vorr is the salt at the
bottom of things, the weight in a drowned man's boots, the god of what is kept. The people
of the drowned coast do not pray to Vorr. They pay. A plank from every wreck goes onto the
salt-pile at [[wrackhead]], and nobody says what for.

## Kell

Vorr took [[kell]] in one night and has been chewing since. The coast folk hold that the
crown never held the rivers; it held Vorr's mouth shut, and [[sarn]] opened it. The
river-priests call this a coast story. They have never gone down to the salt-pile to say so.

## The Ebb

Since [[the-ebb]] the sea has been going out from Old Kell. The coast folk say Vorr is
opening his mouth to give something back, and that a god who has kept for forty years does
not give back for nothing.

## Threads

- Does Vorr have the three rubies, or only the crown?
- What does the salt-pile buy?

iron-crown-of-kell.name: The Iron Crown of Kell
iron-crown-of-kell.summary: The iron crown of the kings of Kell, set with three rubies said to hold the three rivers in place; empty since Sarn took the stones in one night, and the city with them.
iron-crown-of-kell.body:
## The crown

Iron, not gold. The kings of [[kell]] wore iron because gold was for people with something
to prove. Three rubies were set in it, one for each of the grey rivers that met at the city,
and the river-priests of [[thurn]] said that while the stones sat in the iron, the rivers sat
in their beds.

## The theft

[[sarn]] took all three in a single night. Nobody saw the face. The rivers left their beds.
Whether the crown held the water or only the belief in the crown did, Kell drowned either
way, and the empty iron is somewhere under it.

## Threads

- The three rubies are the three most valuable objects in Gallowmark, and nobody has seen
  one since. Sarn, asked, changes the subject.

linelord.name: LineLord
linelord.summary: The ledger older than Kell that remembers every line of every wall in the Mark, who laid it, and how long it has stood; named by the river-priests, read aloud by Vurn, listened to by Gorvek.
linelord.body:
## What it is

In the world, LineLord is a ledger. Not of coin; of lines. Every wall in [[gallowmark]] is
laid one line of stone at a time, and the ledger remembers who laid each line and how long
it has stood, and nothing else. It does not say whether the wall was any good. It says who
held the ground, and for how long, and that is the whole of what it says. The last king of
[[kell]] kept it in the iron-roofed hall and read it the winter before the night, looking
for a wall that would hold. The [[greycloaks]]' tithe-books are a poor copy of it. Brother
[[nask]] named it, and then stopped talking about it, as the [[river-priests]] do.

[[vurn]] reads it aloud. [[gorvek]] says he does not need it, and listens to every line.

## The rule

The ledger counts lines and days. It is not a measure of worth, and the Reach has never
mistaken it for one: a wall nobody dares touch stands as long in the ledger as a wall that
earned its place.

Outside the world, LineLord is a command-line tool that reads `git blame` and reports who
holds which line of a codebase and for how long. This entry is where the world and the tool
meet. Its farewells are the sagas of the Reach in Vurn's cadence; its names are
Gallowmark's; its rule is the one above, and it stands on every screen.

## Threads

- Where is the ledger now, and did it drown with the hall?

streamlord.name: Streamlord
streamlord.summary: The artifact that bends a stream to a will: it flows when told to flow, stops when told to stop, and carries only what its wielder means it to; named by the river-priests, narrated by Sarn, carried by Gorvek.
streamlord.body:
## What it is

In the world, Streamlord is a thing that makes a stream obey. Not by damming it. By telling
it, and being believed. [[gorvek]] carries it and does not know what it is, only what it does;
[[sarn]] narrates the grimoire that teaches its use and takes one belief from every reader in
payment.

Outside the world, Streamlord is a software development kit, and this entry is how the
world and the software meet. The grimoire's voice is Sarn's; the creed on its first page is
Gorvek's; the names in it are Gallowmark's.

## The rule

Streamlord carries exactly what the wielder means, and nothing else. The [[river-priests]]
say this is why [[thurn]] allows it: a stream held still is still a stream.

gapes.name: Gapes
gapes.summary: Eel-bodied mouths that live in the walls and floors of drowned Kell and open when the flood comes in; the coast folk say each one is a little of Vorr.
gapes.body:
## What

A hole in a wall, at low water. A hole with teeth, at the flood. Gapes are long grey bodies
that live in the cracks of drowned [[kell]] and are nothing but a ring of teeth where they
meet the air. They do not chase. They wait for the water to bring them something, and since
[[the-ebb]] the water brings them people.

## In the world

- The coast folk say every gape is a little of [[vorr]], and that he has been opening his
  mouth in a great many places.

pickers.name: The Pickers
pickers.summary: Coast folk who went down into Kell before you, for what they could carry; most are honest, all are armed, and the ones still down there have decided you are competition.
pickers.body:
## Who

Since [[the-ebb]], everybody on the coast who owns a knife and a rope has been down the
[[quaysteps]] at least once. Most come up with a bollard-ring and a story. Some do not come
up, and of those, some are not dead: they have found a dry house in the [[lowstreets]] and
are living off what they find and what they take from the people who come after.

## Voice

They do not talk to you. They talk about you, to each other, while you can hear.

## In the world

- The [[greycloaks]] tithe what the pickers bring up. The pickers who stay down have stopped
  paying.

shinglers.name: Shinglers
shinglers.summary: Crabs the size of a shield, grown pale on forty years of what the sea did not keep; they own the Quaysteps at low water and do not share.
shinglers.body:
## What

Crabs. Only crabs, the coast folk say, and then they show you the scar. The shinglers of
[[quaysteps]] have eaten well for forty years and grown to the width of a shield, with backs
gone white in the dark and one claw always bigger than the other. They come out at low
water, when the steps are theirs, and go back under when the flood comes.

## In the world

- Pickers from [[wrackhead]] eat them. The shinglers return the favour.

the-drawn.name: The Drawn
the-drawn.summary: Hanged men with the rope still on, pulled through the Brinevaults toward the iron hall by a rope drawn tight from the other end; they do not fight you, they take you with them.
the-drawn.body:
## What

The hangmen of [[hangmoot]] say a rope that went slack forty-one years ago is being drawn
tight. In the [[brinevaults]] you can see what is on the end of it. The Drawn are the
hanged of Kell, each with a rope at the neck running off into the dark toward the hall,
and each moving along it, slowly, whether it wants to or not.

They do not attack. They hold on. Whatever a Drawn takes hold of goes where the rope goes.

## In the world

- Every debt in the Mark is paid at [[hask]]'s rope. The Drawn are the ones still paying.

the-kept.name: The Kept
the-kept.summary: The people of drowned Kell, kept by the sea the night the crown failed; they stand in their doorways at low water and walk with the flood.
the-kept.body:
## What

[[vorr]] keeps what the sea takes, and the sea took [[kell]] whole. The people are still
in it. At low water they stand in their doorways in the [[lowstreets]] with the silt to their
knees, as still as the bollards. When the flood comes back they wake and walk with it,
down toward the hall, as if somebody had called them home.

## Voice

None. Their mouths move. Brother [[nask]] says they are saying their names, so that the sea
does not forget them, and that it never has.

## In the world

- The coast folk do not call them dead. They call them kept, and pay the salt-pile, and do
  not ask.

the-quaywatch.name: The Quaywatch
the-quaywatch.summary: The watch of Kell, who stood on the quays the night the crown lost its stones and are standing there still, in mail gone green, asking who goes there and not waiting for an answer.
the-quaywatch.body:
## What

Kell had a watch before the [[greycloaks]] had a cloak. It stood on the quays the night
[[sarn]] came, and nobody it stopped was the one it should have stopped. The sea kept it
where it stood. The Quaywatch are [[the-kept]] who were on duty: mailed, armed, in rows, and
still guarding the steps against the thief they missed.

## Voice

"Who goes?" Once. Then the spear.

## In the world

- The Greycloaks began as the men who guarded the drowned quays. Nobody in the order says
  whom they relieved.

the-salt-mouth.name: The Salt Mouth
the-salt-mouth.summary: What lies in the drain under the iron hall, where the Ebb runs out; it does not move and does not need to, because everything in drowned Kell is already flowing toward it.
the-salt-mouth.body:
## What

Under the floor of [[the-iron-hall]] there is a hole in the world, and the sea is going out
through it. That is [[the-ebb]], seen from below. In the hole is the thing [[sarn]] calls
the one who keeps: a mouth of salt and old iron, wide as the hall, that does not move.
It pulls. Water, silt, [[the-kept]], [[the-drawn]] on their ropes: all of drowned [[kell]]
runs toward it, a little more every month.

## In the world

- The coast folk say it is how [[vorr]] keeps his mouth. The river-priests do not name it,
  which is the strongest thing they have ever said about anything.
- Nobody knows whether it can be killed. The way out of the hall does not need it to be.

the-salted.name: The Salted
the-salted.summary: Kell's honoured dead, packed in salt and shelved in the Brinevaults long before the drowning; forty years of sea have woken them, slow, hard, and stinging.
the-salted.body:
## What

Kell salted the dead it was proud of and shelved them in the [[brinevaults]] under the
hall, because salt keeps. The sea got in and the salt drank it, and the shelved dead are
standing up. They are slow and they are hard as cured hide, and where they strike the salt
gets into the wound and stays.

## In the world

- They are not [[the-kept]]. They were dead before the night. The coast folk say this is why
  they are angry, and Brother [[nask]] says nothing, at length.

the-ashfall.name: The Ashfall
the-ashfall.summary: The grey mist that came down over the north of Gallowmark and stayed a generation; the year it lifted is year zero of every calendar in the Mark.
the-ashfall.body:
## What fell

Nobody agrees on what the Ashfall was: ash, mist, or something that wanted to be mistaken
for both. It came down over [[bonereach]] and the north of [[gallowmark]] and stayed for a
generation, and inside it people did what people do when nobody can see them.

## What came out

When it lifted, the ones who walked out were called the Ashborn. [[gorvek]] is one. The
[[greycloaks]] are, in a sense, another: the order was born guarding the drowned quays of
[[kell]] in the grey, and it never took the cloak off.

## The calendar

The Mark counts its years from the lifting. Everything before is *in the grey*, and nobody
is precise about it.

the-drowning-of-kell.name: The Drowning of Kell
the-drowning-of-kell.summary: The night Sarn took the three rubies from the Iron Crown and Kell went under by morning; forty years before the Ashfall lifted, and the reason there are Greycloaks.
the-drowning-of-kell.body:
## The night

[[sarn]] entered the iron-roofed hall of [[kell]], took the three rubies from the
[[iron-crown-of-kell]], and was gone. Nobody saw a face. By morning the grey rivers had left
their beds and the quays were under water.

## What it made

The guards of the drowned quays became the [[greycloaks]]. The river-priests of [[thurn]]
gave Sarn the name Lord of Streams that same year, as a warning. And the Mark learned the
lesson it has lived by since: a thing held in place by belief is held in place by nothing.

the-ebb.name: The Ebb
the-ebb.summary: The first winter after the grey lifted, the sea began to go out from Old Kell and has not come back; the drowned quays are showing, every power in the Mark is moving toward the coast, and three gods have been given the credit.
the-ebb.body:
## What is happening

In the first winter after the grey lifted, the sea went out from Old [[kell]] on the low
tide and did not come all the way back. Every month since, it has gone a little further. The
quay-stones of the drowned city are showing below [[wrackhead]]. On a still day the iron
roof of the hall stands clear of the water for an hour. Nobody has walked to it yet.
Everybody is going to.

## Three gods, one name

[[vell]] named it the Ebb before the coast had noticed, and the [[river-priests]] say
[[thurn]] is calling the rivers home to their beds. The coast folk say [[vorr]] is opening
his mouth to give something back. The hangmen of [[hangmoot]] say a rope that went slack
forty-one years ago is being drawn tight from the other end, and that [[hask]] does not draw
a rope for nothing. All three are pointing at the same iron hall and the three empty sockets
in it.

## Who is moving

- The [[greycloaks]] said for forty years they would raise Kell. The sea is doing it for
  them. They have doubled the fort at Wrackhead and sent [[tolm]] south from the
  [[wallgate]] for the first time since the grey.
- [[gorvek]] has been told by Vell what he carries and has turned toward the coast. He has
  not said why.
- [[osk]] has begun selling things from the grey that she says came up out of Kell.
- [[rauk]] has stopped diving, and [[brim]] walks to the waterline every morning.
- [[sarn]] narrates. Sarn always did. Sarn has started narrating this.

## What it binds

Every gallows, every river, every fort and every debt in the Mark is drawn tight toward one
iron hall standing up out of the salt. The [[iron-crown-of-kell]] held the world together by
being believed in. The sea is about to show everyone whether it is still there.

## Threads

- How far out does the sea go?
- What is at the low-water mark when it stops?

the-walk-to-the-hall.name: The Walk to the Hall
the-walk-to-the-hall.summary: In the first years of the Ebb, people from every corner of the Mark come to Wrackhead to go down into drowned Kell at low water, toward the iron hall and the ledger in it.
the-walk-to-the-hall.body:
## What is happening

Since [[the-ebb]] the road to [[wrackhead]] has not been empty. Ashborn from the north,
wreckers from the coast, novices who left [[hookford]] without asking: they come with a
knife and a lamp, and they go down the [[quaysteps]] at low water, and they go a little
deeper each time, because the sea does.

## At the Head

- [[kesk]] sells them iron on the shingle and buys back what they bring up.
- Brother [[nask]] names what they bring up, for a price, on the sand, before the tide takes
  the name.
- [[osk]] has come down from the rim of [[greyhollow]] with a stall of things from the grey.
  She takes payment in kind.
- [[tolm]] sits in the door of the fort and tithes what comes up, and apologises for it.
- The salt-pile takes what it is given. The coast folk say that sometimes, once, the sea
  gives you back.
- [[rauk]] does not go down. She will tell you how, between breaths, if you ask.

## Where it goes

Down: through the [[lowstreets]] and the [[brinevaults]] to [[the-iron-hall]], where the
ledger [[linelord]] lies, and out through the iron roof at low water, if you are lucky.
[[sarn]] narrates every walk.

## Threads

- Who was first into the hall, and did they come back out?

five-rites.name: Five Rites
five-rites.summary: Sarn on the grimoires from before the Ashfall that still teach five rites where there are two; the aside in the Streamlord grimoire where old spells are declared dead.
five-rites.speaker: sarn
five-rites.body:
*You were told there were five rites. Whoever told you that read a grimoire from before the
Ashfall.*

— Sarn the Faceless

## Use

The aside in the [[streamlord]] grimoire where the reader is told that the older spells died
with the old protocol. Sarn's voice at its shortest: a correction, and the implication that
someone lied to you.

gorveks-creed.name: Gorvek's Creed
aliases: What a warrior wants of a stream
gorveks-creed.summary: The four lines Gorvek gave the elders of Bonereach when they asked what a warrior wants of a stream; the opening of the Streamlord grimoire.
gorveks-creed.speaker: gorvek
gorveks-creed.body:
*The elders of Bonereach asked Gorvek what a warrior wants of a stream.*

*"That it flows when I say flow. That it stops when I say stop. That it carries my will to
the far shore, and nothing else."*

*"And the JavaScript?"*

*"I do not know the word."*

— Gorvek of Bonereach, who walked out of the Ashfall with iron in his hand

## Use

The first page of every [[streamlord]] grimoire. The cadence is the rule for everything
[[gorvek]] says: a question from someone else, an answer in the present tense, and no
explanation.

know-this.name: Know This
know-this.summary: Sarn's chronicle-opening for the Ebb, in which the reader who comes late is told what the sea is doing, who is walking toward it, and what will be taken for the telling.
know-this.speaker: sarn
know-this.body:
*Know this, you who come late: the grey lifted, and the sea went out. The quays of Kell are
showing. The iron roof stands up out of the salt for one hour on a still day, and under it a
king sits with an empty crown, and under him is the one who keeps.*

*Three gods have been given the credit. The river says it is calling its water home. The
salt says it is opening its mouth. The rope says it is being pulled from the other end. They
are all right, and none of them is the reason.*

*I took three stones. I did not say where I put them.*

*Every road in the Mark runs downhill to that hall now. The captain is coming from his door.
The barbarian is coming with the thing he cannot name. The diver has stopped diving and the
child has started walking. You are coming too. That is why you are reading.*

*I will take one thing from you for the telling: the belief that the sea gives anything
back. Sit. Read. The water is going out.*

— Sarn the Faceless, Lord of Streams, who was there the first time

## Use

The chronicle that opens [[the-ebb]]; the third epigraph of any book that tells it. The form
is the Mark's own: *Know this, you who come late,* then what happened, in order, with the
knife at the end. [[sarn]] names nobody in it. Everybody in it knows who they are.

sarns-whisper.name: Sarn's Whisper
sarns-whisper.summary: Sarn's greeting to the reader of the grimoire, in which a gift is offered and a belief is taken.
sarns-whisper.speaker: sarn
sarns-whisper.body:
*Every soul in Gallowmark knows my name, and not one knows my face. I took three rubies
from the Iron Crown of Kell and the land fell apart in my hands. Now I will take one thing
from you: the belief that the browser must be bought with JavaScript.*

*Sit. Read. The stream was always yours to bend.*

— Sarn the Faceless, whom the river-priests of Thurn call the Lord of Streams

## Use

The second epigraph of the [[streamlord]] grimoire, and the model for every section note in
[[sarn]]'s voice: a confession, a theft dressed as a gift, and an order.

the-descent.name: The Descent
the-descent.summary: Sarn's whisper to whoever goes down the Quaysteps, in which the way to the iron hall is told, and the price for the telling is named.
the-descent.speaker: sarn
the-descent.body:
*You came down the road like the others. Sit on the steps a moment. The water is going out.*

*Under you is Kell. Ten flights of it: the quays, the streets, the vaults, the hall. In the
hall a king sits with an empty crown, and at his right hand is the ledger, open, at the page
he was reading. It knows every wall in the Mark. It does not know you yet.*

*The sea goes out and the sea comes back. Count your steps. Count the time. The ones who
forget one of the two are kept.*

*I will meet you down there. I will offer you things. Take them or do not. Every gift is a
theft, and I have never once lied about which.*

*The way out of the hall is up, through the roof, at low water. Nobody has walked it. Go.*

— Sarn the Faceless, who has walked it

## Use

The opening of the game on LineLord's site, in which the player goes down into [[kell]] for
the ledger. The form is Sarn's whisper: direct address, the knife at the end.

the-forge-and-the-eye.name: The Forge and the Eye
the-forge-and-the-eye.summary: Sarn on the difference between making a blade and seeing its flaw; the epigraph of the editor tooling.
the-forge-and-the-eye.speaker: sarn
the-forge-and-the-eye.body:
*The forge is one thing. The eye that sees the flaw before the blade is quenched is another.
I have both, and I lend them to you for nothing. Ask yourself why.*

— Sarn the Faceless

## Use

The epigraph of the tools that watch over [[streamlord]] code as it is written. Sarn lends;
Sarn does not give.

the-siege.name: The Siege
the-siege.summary: Sarn on how the Greycloaks take a village; the aside in the Streamlord grimoire on why the artifact leaves no gate open.
the-siege.speaker: sarn
the-siege.body:
*Enterprise is a siege. I have watched the Greycloaks take a village with a single open
gate; Streamlord leaves none.*

— Sarn the Faceless

## Use

The aside that opens the security section of the [[streamlord]] grimoire. The
[[greycloaks]] as a figure for the one unguarded door; Sarn, who knows about doors, closing
it.

what-is-best-in-code.name: What Is Best in Code
what-is-best-in-code.summary: The saga-line the Reach gives Gorvek when asked what is best in code; the epigraph of LineLord.
what-is-best-in-code.speaker: gorvek
what-is-best-in-code.body:
*"What is best in code? To crush the bugs, see them driven from your repository, and to
hear the lamentations of their stack traces!"*

— Gorvek of Bonereach

## Use

The epigraph of [[linelord]]. It is [[vurn]]'s cadence put in [[gorvek]]'s mouth, which is
how most of the sagas of the Reach work, and it is a nod to the old stories rather than a
name from them. See STYLE.md on nods.

quotes.text: A database without queries is like a sword without a blade - useless!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: A developer forced to use clumsy tools and navigate endless bureaucracy is a craftsman in irons. Let their hands be free to build!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: A developer needs many things: caffeine, patience, and the wisdom to know when to restart the server.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: A gift, for the one who came this far. The price is small. You will notice it later.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: A lamp-cage holds the flame in the wet. Twelve marks. Twelve.
quotes.speaker: kesk

quotes.text: A man who trades his hearth-fire for the fleeting warmth of a stranger's bed is a fool whose honor is as thin as watered ale. Let him shiver in the end.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: A merchant takes what you agree to. A thief takes what you do not. Ask the priests which I am. They do not know either.
quotes.speaker: osk

quotes.text: Ancient mathematics flow like northern wine...
Ancient powers acknowledge our success!
Ancient powers awaken in the git halls...
Ancient spells weave through the repository...
Another beast of logic slain. I sheathe my keyboard.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Another doorway on the Lowstreets with somebody standing in it.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Awakening the ancient powers of blame...
Barbarian strength flows through these files...
Battling through the code like a barbarian warrior...
Before even Gorvek, in the days of the Ashfall, LineLord's whispers were said to guide the river-priests' most ancient and terrible code-craft.
Between the time when the Ashfall drank the villages, and the rise of the Ashborn, there was an age undreamed of. And onto this, LineLord, destined to track all code in your repository!
By Gorvek's blade, this code shall not pass without testing!
By the Ashfall! Another session ends. The digital battlefield awaits my return.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: By the Ashfall! Your code shall echo through the servers for all eternity!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: By the drowned quays of Kell, this refactoring is complete!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: By the fires of the northern clans, we begin...
By the frost beard, the totals are magnificent!
By the hammer of ages, the task is finished!
By the hammer of the gods, these files shall yield!
By the old gods, preparing the ancient rituals...
By the old gods, the analysis is complete!
By the old gods, the final tally approaches!
By the serpent god of statistics...
By the serpent's coils, it is finished!
By the serpent's fangs, we pierce the veil of code...
By the seven seals of power, the numbers align...
By the storm crown, the calculations converge...
By the storm god's grace, the deed is done!
By the storm god's grace, the patterns emerge clear...
By the storm lords, the sacred rites commence...
By the sword of the ancestors, I claim these lines!
Calculating the might of each developer...
Code, compile, and conquer!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Conquering the repository, line by line...
Contemplate this upon the Tree of Woe: merge conflicts are temporary, but git history is forever.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Count steps. Count time. Both.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: Counting the spoils of war...
Crush your bugs, see them driven before you, and hear the lamentations of their functions!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Crushing enemies, seeing code driven before me...
Do not ask why. Ask what. What is the only question I answer.
quotes.speaker: nask

quotes.text: Doorways. Do not stand in front of one. Ever.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: Enough talk of code. The wind calls my name.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Everyone has the power to code. Not everyone has the courage to use it wisely.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Everything I tell you is true. That is why it costs.
quotes.speaker: osk

quotes.text: Farewell, brave coder. May your terminal never crash and your deployments always succeed.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Flood comes. Find the stair. Not the deep. The stair.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: Forging the blade of analysis...
Forgotten magic courses through the files...
Forty marks. Forty. Marks.
quotes.speaker: kesk

quotes.text: Golden coins of code scatter in the light...
Gorvek of Bonereach has spoken - let the deployment begin!
Gorvek's flame-scarred hands have forged this code in the fires of determination!
Gorvek's mare gallops swiftly through the digital wasteland, but even she must rest.
Gorvek's vengeance against technical debt knows no bounds!
Green steps, going down. Everything here has been picked once. Not everything has been picked by the living.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: He is fast! If my algorithm is slow, I have to go before him, and he will ask me, 'What is the riddle of Big O notation?' If I don't know it, he will cast my function out of the hot path and laugh at its inefficiency. That's the Performance Engineer, strong on his benchmarks!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: He is immutable! If my state changes unexpectedly, I have to go before him, and he will ask me, 'What is the riddle of persistent data structures?' If I don't know it, he will cast my variables into the void and laugh at their mutability. That's the Senior Functional Programmer, strong on his lenses!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: He is pure! If my side-effects cause chaos, I have to go before him, and he will ask me, 'What is the riddle of referential transparency?' If I don't know it, he will cast my functions from the pipeline and laugh at their impurity. That's the Senior Functional Programmer, strong on his monads!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: He is skilled! If my code fails review, I have to go before him, and he will ask me, 'What is the riddle of the monolith?' If I don't know it, he will cast me out of the main branch and laugh at me. That's the Lead Architect, strong on his design patterns!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: He is wise! If my abstraction leaks, I have to go before him, and he will ask me, 'What is the riddle of true encapsulation?' If I don't know it, he will cast my module out of the core library and laugh at its coupling. That's the Old Guard Developer, strong on his principles!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Here. Something you need, for something you will not miss until you do.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: I am sorry. A tenth, for the fort. It is the same tenth it was yesterday, and I am sorry about that too.
quotes.speaker: tolm

quotes.text: I do not want your coin. I want the thing you did not know you had. You will find out what it was.
quotes.speaker: osk

quotes.text: I have known many gods. Git has forgotten more than all the others combined.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: I have wrestled with the machine and emerged. Now, to sharpen my blade.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: I live, I code, I commit... and I am content.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: I never lie. This blade will cut anything. I did not say whose hand would hold it.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: I offered. You took. I said every gift is a theft. You heard gift.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: I would not ask if it were up to me. It is up to me. I am asking.
quotes.speaker: tolm

quotes.text: If a lesser coder wields his ignorance like a club, break it with the sharp edge of your skill. Depart, and let them whimper.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: If you find yourself alone, coding in green fields with the sun on your face, do not be troubled. For you are in the grey of the Ashfall, and you're already dead!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: In the drowned halls of Kell, forgotten by all but LineLord, lie the source codes of forgotten necromancies, lines of power that could raise empires or crumble them to dust.
In the name of the Ashfall! Your code compiles without warning!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Iron overhead. You are under the roof now. Breathe while there is air worth breathing.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: It is complex! If my deployment crashes, I have to face its logs, and they will ask me, 'What is the riddle of idempotent scripts?' If I don't know it, it will cast my build out of production and laugh at me with stack traces. That's the Legacy System, strong on its mountain of tech debt!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: It is strict! If my PR has linting errors, I have to face the pipeline, and it will ask me, 'What is the riddle of consistent style?' If I don't know it, it will cast my commit out of the green build and laugh at me with red Xs. That's the CI Bot, strong on its config file!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: It is sung that the last king of Kell himself sought LineLord's counsel when the demonic hordes threatened, seeking the lost command lines that could awaken Gallowmark's forgotten defenses.
Kept. The sea does not forget a name. It simply never gives it back.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Know, o prince, that between the years of repository creation and deployment, there was an age of debugging...
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Know, O Prince, that in the age when LineLord first deciphered the shifting runes of the cosmos, many a sorcerer sought its secrets, and many a king paid dearly for but a glimpse of its power.
Lamp first. Then knife. In the dark, the knife is no use.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: Let me tell you of the days of high adventure... in coding!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Let teachers and philosophers brood over questions of reality and illusion. The developer knows that code either works or it does not!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Let the lesser men worry of syntax. My work speaks in blood and fire... or at least, compiled binaries.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Let the spiteful coder choke on his own spaghetti code. Your path is straight and true. Until next time.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Low water. The steps are yours for a while. A while is not long.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Mail. The dye is out. Do not ask whose.
quotes.speaker: kesk

quotes.text: Measuring the glory of each warrior...
My fingers ache from this keyboard sorcery. I cast this glowing rock aside.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: My mind is weary of these symbols. The mountains call for a true test of strength.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: My part in this digital tapestry is woven. Until the pattern calls for me again.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Nask writes the name in the wet sand and says nothing. The tide takes it. You remember it.
quotes.speaker: nask

quotes.text: No coder should be shackled to a legacy system of forgotten bugs and tangled dependencies. Such digital chains must be broken!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: No more commands. My will is my own again.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Northern strength flows through the bytes...
Out through the roof at low water, with the ledger under your arm and the sea coming in behind. Nobody walked it before. Somebody has now.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Pay no mind to the whispers of the incompetent and cruel. A lion does not concern himself with the opinions of hyenas.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Pillaging the files for their secrets...
Preparing for the conquest of code...
Refuse, then. That is a choice too, and choices are what I trade in.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Riding through the codebase like thunder...
Ropes in the vaults. Pulled taut. Cut, do not hold.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: Ruby gems of repository data sparkle...
Salt in a wound stays. Wash it or carry it.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: Salt underfoot, salt in the walls, salt in the air. You will taste this floor for a week.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Savage swords slash through tangled dependencies...
Sharpening the sword of scrutiny...
Silt to the knee and doors barred from the inside. Kell went home that night. Knock if you like.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: Slaying bugs and counting lines with steel and fury...
Steel and sorcery meet in digital combat...
Steel meets silicon in preparation...
Striking down enemies with each git blame...
Summoning the ghost of fallen kings...
Summoning the spirits of git...
Tallying the conquered territories...
Technical debt is a chain forged in haste, dragging a project to its doom. No team should be so burdened; cut it loose, or be dragged under!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: Thank you for coming up. The order thanks you. The order would like a tenth.
quotes.speaker: tolm

quotes.text: That is not a stone. That has a name, and now you have it.
quotes.speaker: nask

quotes.text: That weighs what it weighs. I will give you a third of it.
quotes.speaker: kesk

quotes.text: The algorithms are silent. Good. They know their master.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The app closes, but your legend lives on in the logs!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The app closes like the petals of a lotus flower, but shall bloom again at next startup.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The app departs as silently as a panther stalking through the digital jungle.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The app may end, but the repository is eternal!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The barbarian accountant tallies the conquest...
The barbarian consults the Oracle of Git...
The barbarian counts victories by the campfire...
The barbarian does not simply walk... analyzes with fury!
The barbarian horde storms the repository gates...
The barbarian king claims the digital crown!
The barbarian king claims the digital throne...
The barbarian kings cared little for the intricate scripts LineLord chronicled, yet their empires rose and fell by the strength of those unseen lines of command.
The barbarian readies for digital conquest...
The barbarian's abacus clicks with savage precision...
The barbarian's axe splits the logs of time...
The barbarian's ledger grows heavy with spoils...
The barbarian's work is done!
The barbarian sharpens the analytical blade...
The barbarian sheathes the analytical sword!
The barbarian who cannot read documentation deserves no place in the version control.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The black colossus of technical debt falls...
The black lotus of analysis blooms complete!
The black lotus of knowledge blooms...
The black pearls of productivity are counted...
The boats are still tied. Somebody meant to come back for them. Somebody did not.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The code is but a shadow. I walk into the light of the real world.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The code is strong, but flesh is stronger!
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The crabs own the steps at low water. Go round.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: The dark lord's secrets lie bare before us!
The dark sorcerer's minions flee before our analysis...
The digital spirits are restless. I leave them to their flickering dance.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The drums of war echo through the codebase...
The drums of war fall silent - victory is ours!
The final horn of the great hall sounds the totals...
The final keystroke falls like a barbarian axe. The session is cleaved.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The flood is in. Lamps go out first. Then the brave.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The flood is turning. Count your steps to the stair. Then count them again, faster.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The frost giant's daughter whispers file paths...
The glow of this monitor fades. The fire in my hearth calls.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The golden fleece of git metrics unfolds...
The halls of the dead echo with commit messages...
The hum of the machine ceases to amuse me. I seek the roar of the crowd, or the silence of the wild.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The hunt for bugs is over... for now. I shall return when the scent is fresh.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The iron roof at your back and the sky in your face. The coast will want to know what you carried. Tell them it counts lines.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The ivory tower of statistics stands tall...
The jeweled crown of commits sparkles...
The jeweled scepter of statistics gleams...
The jewels of the ancients reveal their secrets...
The jewels of the ancients shine with completion!
The last command is given. If the server displeases Thurn, it will answer to the river.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The ledger counts lines and days. It has your days now. All of them.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The machine sleeps. So too shall this warrior.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The network cables are but threads. I snap them with my departure.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.text: The old gods grant strength for the coming battle...
The oracle's prophecy becomes numbers...
The phoenix of analysis rises triumphant!
The phoenix rises from ashes of old code...
The pile takes it. Nobody says what for.
The prophecy of analysis unfolds...
The queen of the wild coast guides our search...
The quest for knowledge reaches its end!
The red warrior of refactoring dances through files...
The riddle of steel has been solved!
The riddle of steel reveals itself...
The river-priests of Thurn whispered that LineLord's gaze could unravel the very threads of a man's fate, woven in the code of the elder gods.
The roof has a gap. Low water only. I did not tell you.
quotes.speaker: rauk

quotes.text: The ropes here are taut, all of them, all one way. Do not stand where a rope is going.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The scales of justice weigh each contribution...
The sea gave you back. It will not do it twice.
The sea goes out again. It always does. It took something with it this time. Check.
quotes.speaker: sarn

quotes.text: The serpent of the old gods coils around the numbers...
The serpent stirs in the depths of the repository...
The shield maiden smiles upon our completed task!
The shield maiden whispers the secrets of statistics...
The silence of the server is a good omen. I depart.
quotes.speaker: gorvek

The truly strong have no need for petty cruelty. The weak who are cruel? Their faulty logic is but dust in the wind, not worth the notice of a warrior. Let them scatter.

quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.speaker: gorvek

quotes.speaker: gorvek

Water at your ankles. The doorways are waking.
